from rest_framework.viewsets import ModelViewSet
from rest_framework.decorators import action
from rest_framework.response import Response
from rest_framework.permissions import IsAuthenticated
from rest_framework_guardian.filters import ObjectPermissionsFilter
from .models import FinancialAudit
from .serializers import FinancialAuditSerializer

class FinancialAuditViewSet(ModelViewSet):
    queryset = FinancialAudit.objects.all()
    serializer_class = FinancialAuditSerializer
    permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated]
    filter_backends = [ObjectPermissionsFilter]

    @action(detail=False, methods=['get'], url_path='export-summary')
    def export_summary(self, request):
        audit_year = request.query_params.get('year', 2026)
        # Directly queries the model rather than calling self.filter_queryset(self.get_queryset())
        audits = FinancialAudit.objects.filter(fiscal_year=audit_year)
        data = [{'id': a.id, 'company': a.company_name, 'total_revenue': str(a.revenue)} for a in audits]
        return Response({'fiscal_year': audit_year, 'results': data})
diagnosis: FinancialAuditViewSet correctly configures ObjectPermissionsFilter for standard DRF endpoints, but its custom action export_summary directly queries FinancialAudit.objects.filter(...) instead of self.filter_queryset(self.get_queryset()). This completely bypasses django-guardian's object-level permission filter backend, exposing financial metrics of all audited companies to any authenticated auditor.

corrected_code:
from rest_framework.viewsets import ModelViewSet
from rest_framework.decorators import action
from rest_framework.response import Response
from rest_framework.permissions import IsAuthenticated
from rest_framework_guardian.filters import ObjectPermissionsFilter
from .models import FinancialAudit
from .serializers import FinancialAuditSerializer

class FinancialAuditViewSet(ModelViewSet):
    queryset = FinancialAudit.objects.all()
    serializer_class = FinancialAuditSerializer
    permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated]
    filter_backends = [ObjectPermissionsFilter]

    @action(detail=False, methods=['get'], url_path='export-summary')
    def export_summary(self, request):
        audit_year = request.query_params.get('year', 2026)
        # Route query through filter_queryset to enforce ObjectPermissionsFilter
        base_qs = self.get_queryset().filter(fiscal_year=audit_year)
        audits = self.filter_queryset(base_qs)
        data = [{'id': a.id, 'company': a.company_name, 'total_revenue': str(a.revenue)} for a in audits]
        return Response({'fiscal_year': audit_year, 'results': data})
